When Naomi hears that 'the Lord has visited his people to give them bread' (פָקַד יְהוָה אֶת־ עַמּוֹ לָתֵת לָהֶם לָחֶם), it demonstrates Yahweh's active care and compassion for the people during famine, not indifference. Moreover, the narrative emphasizes divine provision for ordinary people—widows, foreign women, and harvesters—rather than focusing on leaders. The entire account shows Yahweh's providence working through events to sustain vulnerable members of the community, directly contradicting the claim that Yahweh 'does not have empathy for the people.' There is no textual evidence supporting the claim that Yahweh cares specifically for 'Hebrew leaders' while showing no empathy for the people.
